title: In 1984, NASA sent 3,301 bees to space to see how they built honeycomb
content: Thousands of honeybees traveled into space aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery in 1984.  These bees were sent to microgravity to see if they could survive and build their famous honeycomb.  Initially, some bees crashed into walls, but they adapted within days.  By the mission's end, the bees flew normally and built about 200 cm of honeycomb.  Most bees survived, and the queen laid eggs which did not hatch after returning.

title: GPS can't work everywhere, so scientists test navigation using cosmic rays
content: Japanese scientists are testing a new navigation system using cosmic ray muons. This system can work in places where GPS signals are unavailable, like underground. Muons can penetrate dense materials, which GPS signals cannot do effectively. Researchers have demonstrated this technology's potential for guiding robots and vehicles. The technology is still under development and requires further refinement for widespread use.

title: Cash buyers dominated the US housing boom. Now financed buyers are fighting back
content: Cash purchases in the US housing market are decreasing significantly.  This trend emerges as home sales slow and inventory levels rise.  Price growth has also moderated considerably, benefiting financed buyers.  Financed buyers are now winning competitive bidding situations more frequently.  Cash buyers are becoming less dominant as the market stabilizes.

title: Rhode Island woman left family farm to become a 300-acre wildlife sanctuary
content: Mabel Norman Cerio turned her 1908 purchase of Paradise Farm in Middletown, Rhode Island, into a lifelong connection with art, wildlife and conservation. An artist and birdwatcher, she planned a bird sanctuary during her lifetime and later left the property to the community through her trust. After her death in 1949, the land became the Norman Bird Sanctuary, which today protects 300 acres of coastal habitat, six miles of trails and diverse wildlife. Her legacy also includes her paintings, sculpture interests and historic links to artists in Europe.

title: A $1 million watch, only 7 of them, and 3 words Sam Altman wanted engraved inside

Based on Vanguart's titanium Orb, which starts at $180,000, each carries the phrase COMPUTE IS DESTINY on the rotor and a line of Python code on the caseback. The Sam Altman watch is part of a wider Silicon Valley trend, with OpenAI, Google, Palantir and Uber staff commissioning custom Tudor timepieces.

title: Villages washed away as massive flash floods tear through Nepal - watch
content: A sudden cloudburst triggered severe flooding in the Bhotekoshi River, devastating Nepal's Rasuwa district. Tragically, at least eight people have lost their lives, and several others remain unaccounted for. The disaster has wreaked havoc on local markets, roads, and bridges. Rescue teams are in full swing, employing helicopters from the Nepal army. Authorities are urging residents living near riverbanks in multiple districts to remain vigilant and prepared.

title: Builder told to pay Rs 6 cr to housing society over delay in occupation certificate

Members faced demolition risk and lived without essential services. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered the builder to rectify this. The builder must also obtain the occupation certificate within twelve months.

title: Rs 30 lakh a month for an intern? India’s trading firms are in a fierce talent war

This surge in hiring is influenced by stricter regulations on derivatives and a lull in equity market movements. Companies such as Quadeye and Graviton Research Capital are notably enhancing their internship packages, with global firms following suit to secure top quantitative talent from leading institutions.

title: How do navies hunt submarines? NATO's deadly game of detection beneath the waves
content: NATO navies are focusing on submarine detection and neutralization challenges.  Exercises like Northern Viking 26 highlight coordinated anti-submarine warfare efforts.  Modern warfare relies on advanced acoustic technology and persistent coordination between assets.  India is the only nation to sink a submerged submarine since World War Two.  Submarine and anti-submarine systems continue to advance, making submarine kills more difficult.

title: Why India’s rice exports to Iran may survive Trump's sanctions threat
content: India's rice exports to Iran are expected to continue despite tougher US sanctions.  Demand from Iran remains firm for food security reasons, ensuring continued purchases.  Indian exporters utilize alternative payment channels in countries like Turkey and the UAE.  Essential goods like rice and pharmaceuticals are unlikely to face disruption.  Bilateral trade has significantly declined from its previous peak levels.

title: Kelli Finglass opens up on possibly leaving Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders

Finglass also acknowledges that retirement could eventually become a personal decision, with family and the possibility of becoming a grandmother potentially guiding her toward a new chapter.

title: Bella Mir suffers first MMA loss to Alex Apodaca in historic DWCS upset

The agreement covers design, development, manufacture, and lifecycle support. This collaboration marks a significant step towards self-reliance in aero-engine technologies. The Aravalli engine will also find applications in civil aviation missions.

title: North American crayfish introduced to Britain now threaten native species
content: signal crayfish (Pacifastacus leniusculus) were brought into the uk from north America in the 1970s . they were intended as a commercial species for restaurants and local markets . but the plan backfired: the hardy invaders escaped into rivers, multiplied rapidly and spread across England, Wales and Scotland .

title: 'Questions don't stop with batons': Rahul attacks Bihar govt over BPSC protests
content: Rahul waded into the escalating BPSC row, questioning the govt . he referred to the police crackdown on protesting students, saying, "questions don't stop with batons" he then targeted the long-standing BJP-JD(U)-led government .

title: US pauses fresh military action against Iran, turns to sanctions and maritime pressure
content: secretary of state Marco Rubio has informed the foreign ministers of several allied countries . instead, the Trump administration plans to intensify pressure on Tehran through other measures . officials stressed that the US has not ruled out military action if Tehran strikes first .

title: House price growth slows to 3.6% in Q1 FY27, says RBI; what’s driving the moderation
content: the all-India house price index rose to 117.5 in Q1 FY27, from 116.2 in Q4 FY26 and 113.4 in the year-ago quarter . on a quarter-on-quarter basis, the index increased 1.1 per cent . however, the slower annual growth suggests that the sharp momentum seen in some housing markets has eased .

title: 'Stand in solidarity': PM Modi speaks to Nepal's Balen Shah, offers flood aid
content: the floods swept through northern Nepal on Wednesday morning after the Bhote Koshi River surged, reportedly from the direction of Tibet . prime minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences over the loss of lives in devastating floods in Nepal .
